duration: I would say most of my adult life.  As a youngster I had little exposure to anyone outside of my cultural frame of reference but later had occasion to meet and be friendly with people from various backgrounds.
disclosure_text: My first career was as a chef, and I hired many new Canadians, more than a few were refugees.  Later I switched to high tech, rising to management fairly quickly.  Again, I worked with a very diverse group of people.
micronarrative:
I was disgusted by the reaction of the prominent local figure; the whole white replacement theory shtick turns my stomach. That he incited others to spew this kind of vitriol is rancid icing on a stale cake. The response of the neighbourhood coalition gives me hope that this kind of lunacy is not shared by all and can be countered through reasonable and peaceful means. It's very thinly veiled racism not founded in any kind of scientific fact or sociological study. Other cultures are no threat whatsoever and can open our eyes to new experiences and viewpoints. I am reminded of the toxic nationalism in Germany in the 1930s and 40s.

I frequently engage with other readers in the comment section of a national newspaper. While moderated, this kind of thing sneaks through from time to time. I make a point of calling people out on it. These exchanges are always in English, so speaking of dialects or linguistic registers is not really on point for my example.

While managing a team of IT professionals tasked with a high-profile project, two of my employees requested a flexible schedule so that they could attend Friday prayers. I saw no reason not to accommodate and did so. One of my other employees started grumbling about preferential treatment; it was clear that he had no patience for cultural norms outside of his frame of reference. I arranged a private meeting in my office and explained that I had a duty as a manager to make reasonable accommodations but it went beyond that— as members of a free society, we all need to show respect for fundamental freedoms like religious expression. I then asked if there was anything he needed accommodation on and let him know my door was always open if such a situation should arise.
